elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Rendered grant: "which license extends to the Issuer's Affiliates on written notice to the Servicer". Affiliate coverage exists, albeit in the notice-conditioned fallback formulation rather than an unconditional preferred-level extension.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: The grant runs only to "the Issuer" and "the Issuer's Affiliates"; no contractor/agent (and notably no Successor Servicer, the operative contractor in this structure) is named as a permitted user. To meet this element the drafter must add words such as "and to contractors acting on the Issuer's behalf, including any Successor Servicer".

The inserted grant states no consideration basis and no term: it is neither characterised as paid-up nor given a duration. Because it cannot be determined whether a paid-up licence exists here, the condition can be neither confirmed as applicable nor as inapplicable; the operative text says nothing about perpetuity.

No "irrevocable" (or equivalent) wording appears in the inserted grant, and the licence is not characterised as paid-up. Nothing expressly permits at-will revocation either, so walk-away territory is avoided, but the preferred irrevocability term is absent.

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: The servicing structure contains no subscription licence construct and the inserted grant is not framed as a subscription; however, because the grant has no stated term or termination mechanic at all, it cannot be affirmatively established that the condition is inapplicable.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: "...and is transferable to any successor to the Issuer by merger or acquisition" — transfer to a successor is expressly permitted (limited to the M&A successor formulation).

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: "which license extends to the Issuer's Affiliates on written notice to the Servicer" — exact fallback mechanic (affiliate coverage triggered by written notice to the Vendor).

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: "is transferable to any successor to the Issuer by merger or acquisition" — express M&A successor transferability, with no Servicer-consent condition attached.

reasons: Position-complete at the fallback: both fallback elements are met in operative language (Affiliates on written notice; transfer to an M&A successor), so the redline is sufficient even though the preferred level fails.

Preferred level fails on contractors: the grant names only the Issuer and its Affiliates. To reach preferred, insert "and to contractors acting on the Issuer's behalf, including any Successor Servicer", and add "perpetual and irrevocable" (or a termination-only-for-uncured-material-breach limit) since the grant currently has no stated term or revocation standard.

Minimality holds: the edit converts the single anti-licence sentence in p0346 into a grant and retains the Servicer-favourable carve-out for materials restricted by transfer/assignment restrictions, confidentiality agreements or legal, regulatory, privacy or data protection policies essentially verbatim. No survival tail, expense, remedy, procedure or personnel/access boilerplate was added, and the scope phrase "to service the Receivables" is an inherent part of defining a licence grant rather than an extra requirement.

No duplicate coverage: "Issuer" is a single trust entity and does not itself include Affiliates, so the affiliate extension is not redundant; a separate authorized-personnel edit was correctly omitted.

Intent preserved: the delivery obligations in clause (i)/(ii) (Receivable Files, accounts and records) and the restricted-materials carve-out survive without contradiction, and the grant runs in the correct direction (Servicer to Issuer).

Repair note (non-fatal): confirm that "Affiliate" is a defined term in the Transfer and Servicing Agreement; it was not returned by the definition resolver, and if undefined the inserted "Issuer's Affiliates" would be a dangling term requiring a definition cross-reference.

Practical note for negotiation: because the licence runs to the Issuer only, servicing continuity on a transition depends on the Successor Servicer being able to use it; the contractor language above is the targeted fix and should be offered as the ask before falling back to the current text.
